question: What is the smallest simultaneous subset of the four physical inclusive-triple upper bounds that rules out every pair-compatible complete cover on the archived collective-only runner window?
event_model: Four labelled residual strict blocking events on one fixed closed window; sixteen nonnegative exact-state masses; supplied total, four singles and six pairs; U is empty-state mass; each T_K is inclusive exact-three plus four-way mass; H=sum_K T_K-Q.
frozen_coordinate_rule: Order all sixteen subsets of the four labelled inclusive triples by cardinality and then lexicographic physical speed triples.
For each subset S, impose every physical upper bound T_K<=b_K for K in S and minimize U using exact total/single/pair moments.
Require an exact rational primal and dual certificate for every optimum. For every subset with optimum zero, retain an exact compatible complete-cover countermodel.

Call a successful subset inclusion-minimal only if its optimum is positive and every proper subset has optimum zero. Report all inclusion-minimal successful subsets before applying the frozen cardinality/lexicographic tie break.
The selected coordinate repair is the successful subset with least cardinality, then lexicographic list of physical speed triples. Do not change this ranking after outcomes.
The full four-bound subset must be evaluated even if a proper subset succeeds, because the physical atom distribution gives an exact upper control at U=1/600.
frozen_collective_comparison: Separately impose the single supplied scalar bound H<=99/185440 and minimize U.
Record the identity certificate U+H=C and compare scalar input count with coordinate input count.

Do not call H cheap: charge one supplied scalar at optimization time, while recording that its present exact derivation used all four physical triple durations and Q. No new geometric derivation of H is attempted.

controls.name: strict_16
controls.role: Run all sixteen actual-triple-bound subsets; the known zero upper bound on triple 6/11/16 should recover a one-coordinate repair if the implementation and interpretation are correct. This repair and its sparse predecessor are prior work.

controls.name: doubling_112
controls.role: Pair-only minimum is already positive; the empty subset must succeed and no higher-order subset search is charged or interpreted as needed.

controls.name: tight_13
controls.role: Run all sixteen actual-triple-bound subsets; no duration repair may exceed the physical U=0, while the valid isolated equality at 3/8 remains a separate endpoint certificate.

abstract_comparison: Read the prior symmetric abstract model only to compare quantifiers: every proper zero-triple subset there can coexist with a cover. Do not present its collective identity or countermodels as a new result and do not count it as a fourth physical control.
falsification: A claimed coordinate repair fails if an exact compatible cover satisfies all of its bounds. A positive lower bound greater than the physical U=1/600, a tight13 positive-duration result, or any invalid exact primal/dual certificate invalidates the calculation. A failure of every proper subset is a valid negative result and must not trigger retuning in this investigation.
verification_contract: Primary and separately structured implementations must reconstruct all physical triple bounds exactly, solve the prescribed subset lattice, compare the target with its reflected window, preserve all zero-optimum countermodels, and check endpoints for tight13. The verifier must not import primary functions or accept floating output as proof.
scope: One target representative plus its reflection check and three existing controls. At most 16 target coordinate LPs, 16 strict16 LPs, 1 doubling112 pair LP, 16 tight13 LPs, and 3 pair-zero collective-bound LPs: 52 exact optimizations total. No new speeds, cores, windows, references, alternate-window work, broad scan, +7/+9, outreach, paid compute, main merge or novelty claim.
